data.title: Introducing the New Auto and Auto Code Routers
data.description: The next generation of Auto Router, rebuilt on a new technical foundation, plus Auto Code, a new router specialized for coding work. Both weigh eleven factors per request against live pricing, provider health, benchmarks, and cache state to pick a model and reasoning effort from the model pool your governance policies allow.

data.title: Build an AI Code Reviewer with OpenRouter
data.description: Code reviewers that only read a Git diff have to guess whether a change breaks anything, and their fixes come back as prose you apply by hand. This guide builds a Python reviewer on the OpenRouter Responses API that uploads your changed files into a Linux sandbox, runs checks to confirm each bug, and returns validated patches. A review takes one to four minutes and costs $0.015 to $0.045.

data.title: How to Build Your Own Always-On AI Agent
data.description: An always-on AI agent wakes up on a schedule, checks something with tools, and reports or acts without you asking. This tutorial builds one in TypeScript with the OpenRouter Agent SDK that watches Hacker News, remembers what it has seen across restarts, stops any run at five cents, and waits for your approval before it posts.

data.title: Open-Weight vs Closed-Weight Models: What's the Difference?
data.description: An open-weight model publishes its trained weights, so anyone can run, fine-tune or serve it. A closed-weight model is only available from its maker. We used a year of OpenRouter usage data, our price catalog and benchmark scores to show what that difference changes for cost, providers and quality.

data.title: How Much Does Claude Code Cost? Real Session Costs by Model
data.description: Claude Code is free to install, and what you pay for is the model it calls. We publish the median cost of real Claude Code sessions on OpenRouter by model and session length. This post shows those costs, why the first request costs the most, what a month of use comes to, and how to lower the bill.

data.title: Claude Opus vs Sonnet vs Haiku: Which Should You Use?
data.description: Use Claude Sonnet 5.5 as your default, Haiku 5.5 for high-volume and sub-agent work, and Opus 5.5 for long tasks where a mistake is costly. We compared the three on price, benchmarks, 11 coding tasks with hidden tests and a Claude Code bug fix. All three passed everything, so the difference was cost.

data.title: Guardrails Now Separate Organization Limits from Workspace Defaults
data.description: Admins can now set organization-wide limits, give people different budgets and model access within them, and change each policy on its own. Existing guardrails keep working.

data.title: How to Extract Tables from a PDF with an LLM
data.description: Send a PDF to a model that reads files, with a strict JSON schema for one row, and you get typed rows back, even from scans and tables that run across pages. We tested five routes on five PDFs and found two failures that return a normal response with no error, and the checks that catch them.

data.title: How to Prevent Prompt Injection: 13 Attacks, Tested
data.description: If your app has a model read documents, emails or web pages, anyone who writes in them can try to give it instructions. We ran 25 attacks against four current models with each defense on and off. Labels cut attack emails, but only checking every tool call with Armor stopped all of them.

data.title: Claude 529 Overloaded: What It Means and How to Fix It
data.description: A 529 overloaded_error from Claude means Anthropic's API is out of capacity for the model you asked for, not that your key or plan is wrong. This guide shows how to retry with backoff, send the same Claude model to another provider through OpenRouter, add a fallback model, and stop the error in Claude Code.

data.title: Hit Your Claude Code Usage Limit? How to Keep Coding
data.description: When Claude Code hits your plan's five-hour or weekly limit, you can keep working by pointing it at an OpenRouter API key. You pay per token for the same Claude models, with no usage window. This guide sets it up as a separate command, checks the cost, and switches back when your plan resets.

data.title: How we rebuilt provider routing for better, faster inference
data.description: Our default routing used to send most traffic to the cheapest provider for a model. The new routing algorithm constantly monitors the performance of every provider endpoint to optimize the balance of cost, speed, and reliability for each new request.

data.title: CSAM Screening Across OpenRouter
data.description: OpenRouter will screen all inference requests for child sexual abuse material (CSAM) as they pass through our service. Screening happens in flight, during request processing. Content flagged as potential CSAM may be retained for human review, with reporting and preservation where required by law.

data.title: Private Endpoints: Bring Your Fine-Tuned Models and Capacity to OpenRouter
data.description: Private Endpoints let Enterprise customers route their own fine-tuned models and dedicated deployments through OpenRouter, alongside the public catalog. Private endpoints are only visible within your organization, and requests go through the API your team already uses. Available by request on the Enterprise plan.

data.title: ElevenLabs is now on OpenRouter
data.description: ElevenLabs is now on OpenRouter with 9 Text to Speech and 2 Speech to Text models. Deliver speech with human-like emotion with Eleven v4, give your agent low-latency replies with v4 Turbo, and turn meetings into notes that show who said what with Scribe v2. Here's which model to pick, and one project built start to finish.

data.title: How an AI Sales Agent Saved Our Sales Team 600 Hours a Month
data.description: Rasp gives OpenRouter's five-person sales team about 600 hours a month back, adds room for two more calls a day per rep, and runs for about $30 a day on Ori.

data.title: Server-Side Code Execution Tools for AI Agents, Compared
data.description: A server-side code execution tool runs the model's commands in the provider's sandbox during your API request, so you don't provision or secure a container. OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google run code for their own models. Our openrouter:shell tool runs commands for any model on the Responses and Messages APIs, and our openrouter:bash tool does the same on the Messages API. This article compares the four on runtime, isolation, persistence, and cost, shows a complete request against our sandbox with the output it returned, and describes the jobs that still need a sandbox platform of your own.

data.title: Agent Frameworks Compared: Tool-Calling Schema Handling
data.description: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google each use a different request and response shape for the same tool. Agent frameworks handle that difference in different places. Some translate one definition into each provider's format, some are native to a single provider, and some hand the question to a connector underneath. This article compares six frameworks on schema definition, translation, and MCP support, then shows how OpenRouter normalizes tool calling at the API layer so a model swap is a change to one string.

data.title: LangChain vs CrewAI: Orchestration Compared to OpenRouter-Native Routing
data.description: Multi-model orchestration is three layers. Workflow orchestration is planning, state, memory, and delegation, and LangGraph and CrewAI are built for it. Model routing is choosing a model per call and falling back when it fails, and provider routing is choosing which provider serves that model. OpenRouter does the second two. This article separates the layers, shows the same two-step pipeline in direct OpenRouter calls and in LangChain, and describes when to add a framework, when to use our Agent SDK, and how to put OpenRouter underneath LangGraph or CrewAI.

data.title: Model Router Benchmarks
data.description: We now benchmark model routers side by side across six suites. Our Router Index weighs quality, speed, and cost so you can decide if you need a router and pick the best one for your needs.

data.title: Model Routing for Support Bots: Cheap-First FAQ Handling
data.description: Cheap-first routing sends routine support questions to a small, inexpensive model and escalates selected hard or uncertain requests to a stronger one. This guide compares the three application-side routing patterns, separates what your application owns from what OpenRouter's Auto Router and model fallbacks handle, walks through a support flow with a copyable request, and sets out how to measure escalation rate and cost per resolved ticket.

data.title: Confidence Thresholds for Model Escalation Routing
data.description: Confidence-based escalation keeps most requests on a cheap model and sends only the ones it is unsure about to a stronger one. This guide covers forcing a numeric confidence field with structured outputs, setting the threshold from error rates on your own traffic, tuning it against accuracy, cost, and latency, routing the escalation in your code, and re-tuning it after launch.

data.title: Cost vs. Quality Tradeoff Framework for Agent Models
data.description: The cheapest model that clears your quality bar is usually not the model at the top of a leaderboard. This framework sets the bar for one task, measures cost per quality point across a cheap, a mid-tier, and a frontier model on your own examples, and picks the cheapest one that clears the bar with margin. It uses live catalog prices and the cost each OpenRouter response reports.

data.title: How to Gate Pull Requests on LLM Evals in CI
data.description: A one-line prompt change can ship an agent that tells customers the wrong refund window, and nothing in a normal CI pipeline checks what the model says. This guide builds a fixed eval set for a support agent, a script that exits non-zero below a measured threshold, and a GitHub Actions job that blocks the merge when the pass rate drops.

data.title: AI Agent Regression Testing After a Prompt or Model Change
data.description: An agent's behavior can change when you edit a prompt, swap a model, change a tool schema, or change what retrieval returns. This guide covers the locked case set, the per-case behavioral contract, and how to run the same suite against two concrete model slugs through OpenRouter so the diff shows what the change did.

data.title: Building a Golden Eval Dataset from Production Traffic
data.description: A golden eval dataset is a curated set of production inputs with reviewed expected outputs, versioned in Git and run before every deploy. This guide covers the five steps to build one from live traffic and how to run the same set against many candidate models through one API.

data.title: How to Test Tool-Calling Accuracy in AI Agents
data.description: An agent can call the wrong tool, or call the right tool with the wrong arguments. This guide covers three ways to test each failure mode, a Python harness that grades both, and how to run the same test cases against several tool-capable models through OpenRouter.

data.title: Best Image-to-Video AI Models in 2026: Cost, Resolution, and Control
data.description: If you already have the image a video should start from, the model choice comes down to what has to happen after that frame. We compared the 26 models in our video catalog that accept a starting frame on duration, resolution, frame control, audio, reference inputs, and price per second, then show how to submit an image-to-video job with the TypeScript SDK.

data.title: Manage and de-risk your API keys with new Security Center
data.description: We audited our own OpenRouter account and found over 1,000 active API keys for 85 employees, 168 of them hadn't been used in months. The new Security Center helps you manage and de-risk your API keys with one place to see every key, know which ones are risky and why, clean them up, and lock them to your own network.

data.title: How to Use Jev: Moderation with the Jev API in TypeScript
data.description: A method for putting Jev to work on a new problem, worked end to end on marketplace listing moderation: what stays in code, what Jev sees, how to phrase the questions, and how to turn its probabilities into publish, hold, or reject.

data.title: Batch API: half-price inference by bundling requests
data.description: Send a whole workload in one POST, collect the results within 24 hours, and typically pay half the per-token price. Across 230k+ batches that completed over our two week beta period, the median finished in 7 minutes.

data.title: Is Jev as Accurate as Frontier Models at Classification?
data.description: Claude Opus 5 leads OpenRouter's classification task ranking by spend. We sent the same 3,080 Banking77 utterances to it and to Jev 1.13 through the Decisions API. Opus scored 84.4% to Jev's 81.0%, and Jev answered in 175 ms at $0.11 per thousand requests against 2.3 seconds and $2.42 for Opus.

data.title: What Is Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
data.description: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is NVIDIA's open-weight 30B mixture-of-experts model with about 3B active parameters per token, built for the high-volume execution calls in an agent run. This post covers what the architecture means, how the model compares with Nemotron 3 Ultra, what context and features each OpenRouter endpoint exposes, and how to call it with structured outputs.

data.title: Two Hours of Work That Takes a Week
data.description: For Descript, testing a new model was a couple of hours of work and a week of waiting. The team removed the waiting. Evaluations run in an hour or two now, and nobody has to ask an engineer for time. This post covers the queue, what replaced it, and what changed once evaluation ran several times a week.

data.title: Jev vs LLM-as-a-Judge
data.description: An LLM judge writes a verdict. Jev returns a probability. We graded the same labeled answers and expert-rated summaries with both, and the difference decides which one you should use for a given rubric. Jev matched the LLM judge on agreement at a fifth of the cost and a tenth of the latency, and its probabilities meant what they said. The LLM judge won on the open rubric.

data.title: What Is Jev? TypeSafe's Decision Model Explained for Developers
data.description: Jev reads text and images and returns typed answers with probabilities instead of prose. Here's what that means, live API calls, how to read the numbers, and how to call it with an OpenRouter key.

data.title: Jev vs LLM: When to Use a Decision Model Instead of Generating Text
data.description: Jev returns typed judgments with probabilities. An LLM returns prose. We benchmarked both on 100 support cases through OpenRouter, then wired them together so Jev routes and the LLM writes.

data.title: Image Generation Models Compared: Cost, Edit, Quality
data.description: Image models are priced per token, per megapixel, or per image, so their listed rates do not compare. We sent the same prompt to 20 of them through the Image API, read usage.cost off each response, and tested text rendering, reference-image editing, seeds, and text-plus-image replies.

data.title: Build a Reliable Tool-Calling Agent Loop on OpenRouter
data.description: A tool-calling agent loop sends the conversation and tool definitions to a model, runs the tool calls the model returns, appends the results, and repeats until the model answers or a stop condition fires. This guide builds that loop in TypeScript with the OpenRouter SDK, then adds an iteration cap, repeated-call detection, model fallback, and history controls.

data.title: Does DeepSeek V4 Have Vision?
data.description: DeepSeek V4 is a family of models, and only some of them accept images. This guide maps every V4 slug on our catalog to its input modalities, shows how to send an image to the two that read images, and shows how to put a vision model in front of the text-only ones.

data.title: Case Study: How Descript Took New Models Off the Engineering Queue
data.description: Descript's Underlord video-editing agent runs 13 production models from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and xAI through one OpenRouter integration. Getting a new model through evaluation used to take more than a week. It now takes one to two hours, and the team does it several times a week.

data.title: LLM-as-a-Judge: Score AI Agent Outputs Automatically
data.description: An LLM judge is a second model that scores an agent's output against criteria you write in plain language. This guide explains where a judge fits beside deterministic tests and human review, then shows how to add one to an Ori Eval test, compare candidate models, calibrate the threshold against human-labeled examples, and keep evaluation cost under control.

data.title: OpenRouter Text-to-Speech: API Tutorial in 5 Minutes
data.description: Our OpenAI-compatible speech endpoint puts TTS models from Mistral, xAI, Microsoft, and more behind one request shape. Here's the path from API key to a playable MP3 in cURL, Python, JavaScript, and the OpenAI SDK, plus the response checks that keep JSON errors out of your audio files.

data.title: Zero Data Retention (ZDR): What It Means for AI APIs
data.description: ZDR means an AI provider processes your prompt, returns a response, and doesn't store either one afterward. It's a retention guarantee, not a universal privacy policy. This page explains the boundary, compares ZDR with related controls, and shows how to enforce it at the account, guardrail, or request level.

data.title: OpenRouter Fusion: How It Works and When to Use It
data.description: Fusion is our compound model. It turns one prompt into a short debate among several models: a panel answers in parallel, a judge maps agreement and disagreement, and the calling model writes the final answer. You trade some speed and tokens for quality. This is what it does, what it costs, and when to use it.

data.title: How to Use OpenRouter Presets: Config-as-Code Guide
data.description: A preset is config-as-code for your LLM calls: a named, versioned set of models, system prompts, provider routing, and sampling parameters. Define it once, reference it as @preset/your-slug everywhere, and update every app from the dashboard without a redeploy.

data.title: Nano Banana API: Edit Images with Gemini in Code
data.description: Send a source image and an edit prompt in one request, get the edited image back, and change the editing model by editing a single field. Runnable Python and TypeScript included.

data.title: Seedance 2.5 Review: What It's Best At and When to Use It
data.description: Seedance 2.5 trades resolution for length. It runs to 30 seconds and stops at 720p. We work through what it's best at, what a clip costs at each resolution, how it compares to Seedance 2.0, Wan 3.0, and Veo 3.1 on our own catalog data, and the cases where we'd recommend a different model.

data.title: In-Region Routing: Route inference in the US or EU
data.description: US In-Region Routing is live, joining the EU. Send requests to us.openrouter.ai and their prompts and completions are decrypted only inside the United States and routed only to shared provider endpoints running there, across models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, NVIDIA, Thinking Machines, DeepSeek, Moonshot, and Qwen. Requests served by your own BYOK key go to your deployment's region, which you control.

data.title: Give any model a terminal and files
data.description: The shell server tool gives any model on OpenRouter a hosted Linux shell, and the Files API moves files in and out of it. Commands run in an isolated container, the model reads back stdout, stderr, and exit codes, and files the run writes can be downloaded afterward. Available today in beta on the Responses and Messages APIs.

data.title: How to Choose the Best AI Model (Live, in Your Editor)
data.description: There's no single best AI model, only the best model for a given task, budget, and moment. This article describes a six-step framework for choosing one, and how to run every step from your editor through the OpenRouter MCP server.

data.title: GPT 5.6 Discounts & Jevons Paradox
data.description: OpenAI introduced large discounts on their new Terra and Luna models from July 27th through August 14th. What impact did these discounts have on token volumes, total spend, and the competition?

data.title: OpenRouter Video Generation API: A Code-First Guide
data.description: Every video provider has its own endpoint, job statuses, polling logic, and output format. Our async video API puts Seedance, Veo, Wan, and more behind one submit, poll, and download loop. Here's the full lifecycle in Python and TypeScript.

data.title: Image Benchmarks: See the Capabilities of Every Model
data.description: We ran 39 image models through 15 deliberately hard prompts and put every result on one page. Compare fill levels, finger counts, poster text, and edits side by side, with the price and generation time under each image.

data.title: OpenRouter is Joining Stripe
data.description: Today, we are excited to announce that we are joining forces with Stripe, to power the next wave of GDP growth globally.

data.title: Understand your AI usage: every agent, model, and request
data.description: See what your team spent on every model, save the charts you keep rebuilding, click any bar to land in the logs behind it, and query the same data from your terminal with the Analytics API.

data.title: OpenRouter Image Generation: A Code-First API Tutorial
data.description: Supporting more than one image provider means handling different endpoints, data formats, and billing models. Our dedicated Image API gives you one request format and one key across supported models. Here's the full prompt-to-local-file workflow in Python and JavaScript.

data.title: How to Send an Image to an LLM via API (Vision Guide)
data.description: To get a model to read a screenshot, you need the right request body. This guide shows the content-array pattern that works across every vision-capable model we support, when to use base64 instead of a hosted URL, and how to build multimodal RAG on top of it.

data.title: Tool Calling Across Any Model: Write the Loop Once, Swap the Model String
data.description: Most tool-calling tutorials cover one provider, so you rewrite the loop when you switch. This guide shows the full loop in Python, JavaScript, and cURL, then runs it against three providers by changing one string.

data.title: Live Web Search Benchmarks: Pick the Right Engine, Depth, and Model for Your Agent
data.description: We published live leaderboards grading web search configurations across four task suites. Compare engines, search depth, and models by quality, cost, and speed before your agent makes its first search.

data.title: Model Routing Powered by Wisdom of the Market
data.description: Our new Auto router is informed by the model decisions of millions of people, and it outperforms conventional task-based classifiers across a wide spectrum of tasks.

data.title: Set Up Team AI Spend Controls on OpenRouter
data.description: OpenRouter has five controls for team spend: an organization with a shared credit pool, presets that scope models per workload, per-key spend caps, guardrails that enforce per-member budgets, and the Activity dashboard that shows who spent what. This guide sets them all up in one pass, in order.

data.title: Governing AI Spend Across a Team on OpenRouter
data.description: Your team's AI bill is the total of every key each engineer holds. OpenRouter gives you six ways to control that spend, from per-key limits to Enterprise workspace budgets. This guide explains what each control caps, what plan it needs, and which ones fit your team.

data.title: Ori Harness: The Best Way to Use OpenRouter with Any Harness
data.description: Using OpenRouter with your favorite harness usually means ad-hoc scripts or a wall of environment variables. Install the ori CLI, log in once, and every supported harness runs with an optimized configuration out of the box.

data.title: Ori Eval: Find the Best Model for What You're Building
data.description: Choosing the model inside your product is often decided without a systematic method. Ori Eval answers the question with proof: it runs your agent on your own prompts, checks the tools it called, and grades the answers.

data.title: Using OpenRouter With LangChain: ChatOpenRouter Setup Guide
data.description: The LangChain integration now has a dedicated package: langchain-openrouter on PyPI and @langchain/openrouter on npm. Most guides still teach the old ChatOpenAI base_url override. This is the current path, plus the routing economics the docs skip.

data.title: How to Evaluate LLM Provider Performance Across Latency, Throughput, and Uptime
data.description: The same model behaves differently across provider endpoints. Infrastructure, quantization, load handling, and routing defaults all change the result. Here's how to measure latency, throughput, uptime, and precision, then turn the measurements into a routing policy.

data.title: Image Generation Models: Choosing One, Fixing Errors
data.description: The image catalog covers ten labs and the slugs change monthly. Here's how to narrow it down by job, parameter support, and price, plus what each Image API error message means and how to fix it.

data.title: Classifiers: Track What Your Agents Do and What It Costs
data.description: Define a taxonomy and a small model tags every generation in your workspace by department, task type, or agent complexity. Filter your logs and group your Activity analytics by the results.

data.title: Transcription on OpenRouter
data.description: Send base64 audio to POST /api/v1/audio/transcriptions and get JSON text plus a usage object back, with the same API key you already use for chat. Here's the full request contract, the model families, and the limits to design around.

data.title: The Cheapest Token Is a Cached One: Prompt Caching + Sticky Routing
data.description: Your agent sends the same system prompt, tool definitions, and schemas on every turn. Cache reads cost 0.1x to 0.5x of fresh input, but only if the next request lands on the provider holding the warm cache. Here's how caching and sticky routing work together, and how to confirm they're working.

data.title: Every Modality Through One API
data.description: Chat, image generation, embeddings, and transcription usually mean four SDKs, four bills, and four auth schemes. On OpenRouter every modality runs through one base URL: you change the model string and the content type, and the same routing controls carry across.

data.title: A New Look for OpenRouter
data.description: Built from first principles and grounded in timeless Bauhaus philosophy, our new brand identity marks the beginning of our next chapter.

data.title: Why Use OpenRouter for DeepSeek
data.description: DeepSeek is one model served by 16 providers, at prices that vary by about 4x and throughput from 4 to 57 tokens per second. Here's what routing that spread through one slug actually buys you, and when going direct is the better call.

data.title: Choosing the Optimal Image Input Detail Level in LLMs
data.description: We ran 1,730 visual reasoning questions across 5 models. Dropping image detail to "low" costs real accuracy, and on gpt-5.5 the bill went up too. The lever that reliably cuts cost is reasoning effort.

data.title: DeepSeek V4 Is Earning Agentic Token Share
data.description: DeepSeek doubled its token share on OpenRouter in six months. V4 Flash is the model that made it happen, and agentic workloads are driving the surge.

data.title: The Open Weight Models that Matter: June 2026
data.description: A slew of compelling open-weight models have shipped from new players in both China and the US. As of June 2026, these are the four open-weight models that matter the most — and when to reach for each.

data.title: The OpenRouter MCP Server
data.description: Connect your coding agent to OpenRouter's live model catalog, benchmarks, docs, and test inference, all without leaving your editor.

data.title: Introducing the Unified Image API
data.description: A dedicated Image API with capability discovery across 60+ models from 12 providers. One endpoint tells your code what each model can do.

data.title: AI Governance Checklist: Your LLM Architecture Comes First
data.description: Policy language can't show who called which model or where the audit trail lives. Map your governance checklist to the three routing postures your stack can actually prove.

data.title: How to Enforce AI Data Residency Without Building Local Infrastructure
data.description: If your procurement team flagged country of origin, you don't need to build local infrastructure. For API teams, data residency is a routing constraint you enforce in a single request.

data.title: OpenRouter vs Portkey: Which LLM Gateway for Your Team?
data.description: OpenRouter routes across providers on credits you buy; Portkey governs the provider keys you already have. Here's how they compare on models, observability, compliance, and price.

data.title: OpenRouter vs LiteLLM: Which LLM Gateway Fits Your Stack?
data.description: OpenRouter is a managed gateway; LiteLLM is a self-hosted proxy. Here's how they compare on cost, data residency, routing, and latency.

data.title: Connect OpenClaw to OpenRouter
data.description: OpenClaw has built-in OpenRouter support. One command gives your agents one key, one bill, and automatic failover across hundreds of models. Here's the setup and the fixes for the errors that trip people up.

data.title: How to Connect SillyTavern to OpenRouter (2026 Guide)
data.description: One OpenRouter key gives SillyTavern hundreds of models in a single dropdown, many of them free to start. Here's the five-step connection, the roleplay models to try, and fixes for the errors users hit most.

data.title: Kilo Code + OpenRouter: Setup, Model Routing, and Free Models
data.description: Kilo Code is a bring-your-own-provider coding agent, so adding OpenRouter gives it one key for hundreds of models, provider routing, and failover. Here's the three-step setup plus the kilo.json fields that control routing.

data.title: How to Use OpenAI Codex CLI with OpenRouter
data.description: Codex CLI supports custom OpenAI-compatible providers, so a small config.toml block routes it through OpenRouter. You get provider failover, usage tracking, and one key across every model, with no change to Codex itself.

data.title: How to Use Claude Code with OpenRouter
data.description: Route Claude Code through OpenRouter with three environment variables and no local proxy. You get provider failover, budget controls, and usage visibility on top of the same Anthropic models.

data.title: How to Use OpenRouter With Any Coding Agent or AI Tool
data.description: Any tool that speaks the OpenAI API works with OpenRouter after two changes, the base URL and the key. Here's the setup pattern and the tools that already support it.

data.title: Subagent: Let Your Model Delegate the Busywork
data.description: The openrouter:subagent server tool lets a frontier model hand off self-contained tasks to a smaller, cheaper, faster worker model mid-generation. Summarize a doc, extract structured data, reformat text, all without burning frontier tokens.

data.title: Free LLM APIs Compared: Rate Limits, Models, and Real Costs (2026)
data.description: Stop guessing which free LLM API survives past a side project. Here's how OpenRouter, Groq, Gemini, and 10 more compare on limits, cost, and data use.

data.title: Agentic AI Governance: Your API Key Is a Guardrail
data.description: Most agentic AI governance frameworks define the rules but never enforce them. Learn how the API routing layer stops runaway spend and model escalation.

data.title: Keep Your Agent Running When Models Disappear
data.description: Anthropic restricted Claude Fable 5 just days after launch. If your code hard-codes a model slug, that becomes your outage too. Presets move model choice to the server so you can swap models, set fallbacks, and enforce a data policy without redeploying.

data.title: How to Use Hermes Agent with OpenRouter: Setup, Models & Routing
data.description: Hermes Agent has pushed over 17 trillion tokens through OpenRouter. Here's how to set it up, pick a model that clears the 64K context bar, and tune routing for cost and reliability.

data.title: How to Get the Lowest-Cost LLM Inference on OpenRouter
data.description: Append :floor for the cheapest provider, cap spend with max_price, and start free with 20+ zero-cost models. Plus the billing gotchas to avoid.

data.title: How OpenRouter Model Routing Works
data.description: OpenRouter routes every request across 70+ providers, and you control how: provider order, price ceilings, and the fallback chain. Here's how each routing layer works.

data.title: OpenRouter Reliability & Automatic Failover: How Requests Keep Succeeding
data.description: Provider failover is on by default. Model fallbacks are opt-in. The two layers recover from different failures; here's how each one works and where failover stops.

data.title: Surpassing Frontier Performance with Fusion
data.description: A panel of budget models, fused through OpenRouter, outscored GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.8 on 100 complex research tasks.

data.title: Dinner is Served
data.description: Standardizing on one LLM is like everyone at the table ordering their own entree. The case for going family style with your AI, and the OpenRouter data showing teams already do.

data.title: What Is an LLM Gateway? The Missing Layer Between Your App and AI Models
data.description: Without an LLM gateway, provider outages become user-facing errors and AI spend stays opaque. Compare the best options by routing, compliance, and setup time.

data.title: Advisor: Give Any Model a Lifeline to a Smarter One
data.description: The openrouter:advisor server tool lets a fast, cheap model consult a stronger one mid-generation. Run GPT-4o Mini for the routine work. Call Claude Fable when it actually matters.
